log.why: Test the leading candidate dnaK directly; a positive result will push its posterior above 85% for a fast publication.
Treating at 1 µM splits the cumulative probability mass nearly in half (0.432 vs 0.568), maximizing information gain for Ticket 2.
Test the leading candidate hisG directly; a positive result will strongly confirm it for immediate publication.
E3 tests the 3 µM threshold, evenly splitting the posterior (0.43 vs 0.57) and directly testing the top candidate.
Ticket 1 has a high posterior of 0.872 for hisG after two experiments, making it optimal to publish now and save plates and time.
Test 3 µM on Ticket 3 to split its prior probability mass roughly in half while saving remaining clean plates for unread tickets.
With E2 negative and E3 positive, the posterior for 3 µM is 0.715, high enough to publish profitably without spending another plate.
Test at 10 µM to split the remaining probability mass (59% at or below 10 µM vs 41% above) and potentially confirm 10 µM.
Test the half of the candidate genes containing the top candidate ftsZ to bisect the probability mass.
Test the leading candidate ftsZ (posterior 0.494) to split the remaining probability mass evenly.
Ticket 3 has a strong 0.680 posterior for 10 uM after E3 no-response and E4 response, with only 30s remaining.
Test the trpE and ftsZ pair (combined posterior 0.465) on Ticket 5 so it incubates while we publish Ticket 4 next.
Run E9 on Ticket 5 to cross-reference with growing E5 while incubators are free, before publishing Ticket 4.
Ticket 4 has only 6s left and a strong 0.917 posterior for ftsZ, so we must publish immediately.
Start incubating a direct test of top candidate gyrA on Ticket 7 before publishing Ticket 5 to maximize limited end-of-round time.
Posterior for ftsZ is high (0.865) after E5 and E9, and only 18 seconds remain in the round.
Only 3 seconds remain in the round, so no experiment or publication can finish in time.
